To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the plant breeding community in India has not been able to come out of the traditional breeding methods and has not adopted the modern biotechnology techniques in plant breeding.

1) the plant breeding community in the State Agricultural University and the Indian Council of Agriculture Research institutions in Bihar is not a monolithic group, 2) there are different views on the issues of genetically modified crops, and 3) there is a lack of consensus on the issue of intellectual property rights.
the plant breeding community is not homogenous in its understanding of plant biotechnology and the role that it plays in the development of agriculture in Bihar.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What are the different meanings attached to plant biotechnology by plant breeders in Bihar, India? How do these different meanings get constituted? What are the implications for the future of agricultural research in Bihar and India?

the following issues. How is plant breeding conceived of in India and how does this differ from the conception of plant breeding in the West? What are the implications of this difference for the future of agriculture in India and the world? How does this difference relate to the politics of development and the politics of knowledge production?
the social construction of the plant breeder and the social construction of his/her work.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the plant breeders in Bihar are not only concerned with the production of new varieties of plants but are also engaged in the production of knowledge about plants, plant breeding, and plant breeding practices, as they are situated in the larger socio-economic and political context.

the plant breeding community in India is not a monolithic group, but rather a heterogeneous community, with a variety of interests, values, and beliefs about the role of plant biotechnology in agriculture, and the role of plant breeding in general in the Indian agricultural development process.

the plant breeders in Bihar are not averse to new agricultural technology and are open to the use of biotechnology, provided the benefits of new technology are made available to farmers in a transparent and equitable manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plant breeding community in India is in the midst of a transition, and the new agricultural technology is a part of that transition.
plant biotechnology has been conceived of as an important component of the agricultural research agenda in the state.

, in Bihar, there are a few plant biotechnology enthusiasts who have the potential of becoming a vanguard for plant biotechnology in the state, while a large number of plant breeding community members have been critical of plant biotechnology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plant breeding in Bihar, as in other parts of India, is a complex and multi-dimensional process.

the community of plant biotechnologists is divided on the issue of plant breeding and plant biotechnology, and that the community is also divided on the question of the role of the state in plant breeding research and development.

the plant breeding community is not a homogenous one, but is rather a complex and diverse set of actors, each with its own motivations for and understandings of biotechnology, its applications and the role of the state in facilitating and supporting the development of this new agricultural technology.
